Convention between South Africa and the United States of America for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (1997)
SADC Protocol on Finance and Investment

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001, as amended; Companies Act 71 of 2008 and Companies Regulations 2011, as amended by the Companies Amendment Act 16 of 2023 (Beneficial Ownership Register); Prevention of Organised Crime Act 121 of 1998; Protection of Constitutional Democracy Against Terrorism and Related Activities Act 33 of 2004; General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copy of passport of each non-resident director and shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority in country of origin or notary public

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or financial institution in country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate extract / certificate of good standing, if shareholder is a juristic entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of the shareholder's country

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming source of funds for initial capital contribution
Tax clearance certificate of each foreign director/shareholder (where applicable)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: South African Revenue Service (SARS) or foreign tax authority

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the UN Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, South African Defence and Security Services targeted financial sanctions list, and the Financial Intelligence Centre's risk indicators. Enhanced due diligence is required for Politically Exposed Persons per FIC Guidance Note 4A. The M&A advisory boutique, as a designated accountable institution under the FIC Act, must maintain transaction monitoring and file suspicious transaction reports with the Financial Intelligence Centre.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) Online Services Portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in English or an official South African language; names in non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into Latin characters on the name reservation application. The name must end with the legal form indicator '(Pty) Ltd' for a private company. Words likely to imply official state sponsorship, gross offence, or obscenity are prohibited.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the CIPC rejects a name reservation, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the CIPC within 30 business days of the rejection notice, supplying a corrected name or consent from the relevant Minister for a sensitive token. Alternatively, the applicant may lodge a new name reservation application with payment of the prescribed fee. For prohibited words requiring ministerial approval, written consent from the responsible Minister must be obtained and appended to the reservation application.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for registered office purposes, provided the service provider maintains a physical South African address and does not use a post box. For an M&A advisory boutique, the FIC Act requires a verifiable physical place of business where AML/CFT records, client due diligence files, and audit documents can be retained and inspected.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High (70–85% within the first 24 months of operation) due to FIC Act accountable institution obligations and unannounced compliance inspections by the Financial Intelligence Centre and SARS.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, as amended by the Companies Amendment Act 16 of 2024, particularly ss. 4 (solvency and liquidity test), 13 (incorporation), 14 (Notice of Incorporation), 15 (Memorandum of Incorporation), 17 (company names), 19 (legal capacity), and 66 (board of directors); beneficial-ownership obligations under the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), an agency of the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (dtic)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (CoR 14.1) filed with the Memorandum of Incorporation through the CIPC e-Services portal; the CIPC issues the Certificate of Incorporation (CoR 14.1A) on final approval
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up or authorised capital is prescribed for a private company; shares must be issued for adequate consideration and the board must apply the s.4 solvency and liquidity test before allotment. No escrow deposit or capital lock-in is mandated by the Companies Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF ZA (PTY) LTD - ADOPTED ON [DATE]

1. SHARE SUBSCRIPTION - The board resolves that the initial ordinary shares be allotted and issued to the founding subscriber at ZAR 1.00 per share, fully paid in cash, and records that the statutory solvency and liquidity test under section 4 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 is satisfied.

2. REGISTERED OFFICE - The board adopts [complete street address], South Africa, as the registered office and instructs the incorporation agent to reflect this address in the CIPC records.

3. OFFICERS - The board appoints [Director Name] as Managing Director and [Financial Director Name] as Chief Financial Officer, authorising each holder jointly to operate bank accounts and execute agreements.

Adopted by unanimous written consent of all directors on [date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Availability Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) e-Services portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform a name availability search in the CIPC database and file form CoR 9.1 to reserve up to two proposed company names. A reserved name is held for 2 months. If the incorporator elects not to reserve a name, the company may be incorporated using its enterprise number as the company name.
required_dossiers: Form CoR 9.1 completed and signed
Certified identity document or passport of the applicant/incorporator
Written authority where an agent lodges the application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the CIPC refuses the name as undesirable or confusingly similar to a registered name, file a new CoR 9.1 with alternative names, or proceed with a name-free incorporation using the enterprise number assigned by CIPC.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Signature of the Memorandum of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator acting for the company (filing later made to CIPC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the MOI adopting the standard provisions of Schedule 2 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 or a bespoke MOI covering class rights, pre-emptive rights, director appointment thresholds, and disclosure requirements. Ensure compliance with s.15(2) of the Act and attest the signatures of the incorporator(s). For a boutique M&A advisory with a single class of ordinary shares, the short-form standard MOI may be used.
required_dossiers: Memorandum of Incorporation (standard or bespoke)
Consent to act as director (form CoR 14.3) from each designated director
Power of attorney where signing through a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CIPC queries an MOI provision, file an amended MOI through the CIPC e-Services query-resolution function and pay the applicable correction fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Submission of the Notice of Incorporation to the CIPC
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC e-Services portal - Register a Company workflow
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit form CoR 14.1 online together with the signed MOI and the prescribed incorporation fee. Upon finalization, CIPC issues the Certificate of Incorporation (CoR 14.1A) reflecting the company's registration number, which serves as conclusive proof of incorporation under s.13(4) and s.19 of the Companies Act.
required_dossiers: Notice of Incorporation (CoR 14.1)
Signed Memorandum of Incorporation
Certified copies of identity documents of the incorporator and all directors
Consent-to-act forms (CoR 14.3)
Proof of payment of the CIPC incorporation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected or returned, correct the flagged data and re-submit within 15 business days of the query notice; late re-submission is treated as a new application requiring a fresh fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Shares and Constitution of Statutory Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors of the company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following incorporation, the board issues distinguishing share certificates to subscribers, prepares the issuer-created securities register, and opens the register of directors and the Beneficial Ownership register. Statutory records must be maintained on a continuous basis and filed with CIPC where required, notably the annual beneficial ownership declaration and annual returns.
required_dossiers: Share certificates incorporating the company name, registration number, and class of shares
Issuer-created securities register (share register)
Register of directors and alternate directors
Beneficial ownership register under the amended Companies Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC flags an inconsistency in the Beneficial Ownership data, amend the register and file a corrective return via e-Services; ensure the register is up to date before each annual return submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration with the South African Revenue Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as a taxpayer for income tax through SARS eFiling and obtain an income tax reference number. Assess compulsory VAT registration where taxable turnover exceeded or is expected to exceed R1 million in 12 months, and register for VAT, PAYE, UIF, and SDL once employees are appointed. Maintain a clean initial tax-compliance status for subsequent FSCA licensing.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (CoR 14.1A)
Signed Memorandum of Incorporation
Certified identity documents of directors
Physical business address details
Company bank account confirmation
Completed SARS company registration electronic questionnaires
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS disputes the effective registration date or entity classification, file a request for correction with a supporting board resolution and transaction timeline; appeal the assessment through the SARS dispute-resolution process if necessary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Corporate Bank Accounts under FICA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Selected commercial bank acting under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the corporate account application together with the KYC package. The bank must verify beneficial ownership, directors, and authorised signatories. A board resolution adopting the mandate and signatory limits is required. As a medium-risk M&A advisory boutique, the bank may apply enhanced due diligence to confirm sources of funds and expected transactional flows, especially for cross-border success-fee wire transfers and SWIFT payments.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Memorandum of Incorporation
Board resolution adopting the bank mandate and signatories
Certified identity documents of directors and signatories
Proof of registered office address
Income tax reference number
Beneficial ownership schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the bank requests enhanced due diligence, provide an updated beneficial ownership schedule, client-sourcing profile, and source-of-funds declaration; follow the bank's internal complaint escalation path if the account opening is unreasonably delayed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: FSCA Financial Services Provider Licensing under the FAIS Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Sector Conduct Authority (FSCA), Licensing Division (CATS online portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a Category I Financial Services Provider (FSP) licence before commencing regulated advisory or intermediary services in relation to financial products, including securities and transactions involving the solicitation of investments in equity or debt instruments. The application requires approval of Key Individuals and representatives under the fit-and-proper framework, including the RE 5 regulatory examination and recognised qualifications, submission of a compliance programme with a s.17(1) FAIS compliance officer mandate, and a detailed business plan outlining the M&A advisory function. The FSCA must generally decide within 120 business days of receipt of complete information.
required_dossiers: FSCA FSP application completed on CATS
Memorandum of Incorporation and Certificate of Incorporation
Fit-and-proper questionnaires (FAIS Form 33) for all Key Individuals
Academic qualifications, professional experience records, and continuous professional development evidence
RE 5 regulatory examination certificates for Key Individuals
Compliance manual and s.17 compliance officer appointment
Business plan for the M&A advisory boutique
Police clearance certificates for Key Individuals
SARS tax clearance
Professional indemnity and fidelity cover confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the FSCA issues a notice of intention to refuse, submit written representations within the period stated in the notice, and appeal any final refusal to the Financial Services Tribunal in terms of the Financial Sector Regulation Act 9 of 2017.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration as an Accountable Institution with the Financial Intelligence Centre
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Intelligence Centre (FIC) - GoAML registration portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as an accountable institution under Schedule 1 of the FIC Act because rendering investment-advice or securities-intermediation services triggers an AML/CFT registration obligation. Appoint a compliance officer, adopt a Risk Management and Compliance Programme (RMCP), file the Risk and Compliance Return (RCR) questionnaire, and implement internal procedures for client due diligence, record-keeping, and suspicious-transaction reporting. Registration must precede transactional activity.
required_dossiers: FIC registration questionnaire (own-form submission)
Risk Management and Compliance Programme (RMCP)
Corporate governance and risk framework documents
Evidence of the appointed AML compliance officer
Client identification and verification procedures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the FIC flags an incomplete registration, promptly furnish the outstanding RMCP sections and correct any risk-classification gaps; maintain documentary evidence of the registration date for audit purposes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Trading Licence, Building Compliance, and Employer Fund Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipal licensing and building-control department; Department of Employment and Labour (Compensation Fund and UIF)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Secure municipal approval of the registered office premises as a permissible office use under the town-planning scheme, obtain the electrical certificate of compliance and any fire-safety clearances required by the National Building Regulations, and register as an employer with the Compensation Fund for COIDA and the Unemployment Insurance Fund. These authorisations are conditions precedent to occupying the physical office and engaging staff.
required_dossiers: Municipal occupancy or business licence application
Lease agreement and town-planning use approval
Electrical certificate of compliance (SANS 10142)
Fire-safety clearance certificate
COIDA employer registration confirmation
UIF and SDL registration confirmation (SARS-generated)
Occupational Health and Safety Act workplace risk assessment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality refuses a trading licence on zoning grounds, file a re-zoning or written use-rights application, or relocate the registered office to premises within a commercial zone and re-initiate the licence procedure.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Financial Sector Conduct Authority (FSCA); parallel registration as an accountable institution with the Financial Intelligence Centre (FIC)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Category I Financial Services Provider (FSP) licence under the Financial Advisory and Intermediary Services Act 37 of 2002, together with FIC accountable-institution registration

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE); municipal environmental health departments
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - office-based M&A advisory services do not fall within any listed or specified activity of the EIA Regulations, 2014 (as amended); no Basic Assessment, Scoping Report, or Environmental Authorisation is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to a professional office operation. The company remains subject to the general duty of care under s.28 of the National Environmental Management Act 107 of 1998; municipal solid waste must be disposed through the registered municipal waste stream; any trade effluent from a staff canteen or kitchen must comply with municipal sewerage by-laws (typically pH 6-10 and acceptable BOD/COD limits); heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning systems must comply with the National Building Regulations (SANS 10400) and indoor air-quality requirements of the Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Municipal fire-safety certificate (fire clearance) for the registered office floor or tenant area; electrical certificate of compliance for the installation; structural or professional certification where required under the lease; Occupational Health and Safety Act workplace risk-assessment and incident-reporting protocols; COIDA employer registration with the Compensation Fund; and designation of a health-and-safety representative for premises with more than 20 employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) — national eFiling portal: https://www.sarsefiling.co.za
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: (1) Incorporate the (Pty) Ltd with the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) under the Companies Act 71 of 2008; CIPC issues the enterprise number and COR14.3 incorporation certificate (no minimum issued share capital is required and non-resident ownership is permitted). (2) Through CIPC-SARS data matching, SARS automatically activates a 10-digit income tax reference number (TIN); if no TIN is auto-generated, register via eFiling using the company registration forms. (3) For VAT, file the VAT 101 application electronically once taxable supplies exceed or are reasonably expected to exceed ZAR 1,000,000 within any 12-month period (compulsory registration under s 23(1) of the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991) or apply voluntarily where taxable turnover exceeds ZAR 50,000 (s 23(2)); a non-resident entity carrying on an 'enterprise' in South Africa (frequent or repeated taxable supplies, s 1 VAT Act) is likewise a non-resident vendor and must register for VAT. (4) Submit to SARS: certified Memorandum of Incorporation, COR14.3, director identification and apostilled foreign extract documents, proof of physical business address, and bank confirmation details; appoint a full-time 'public officer' resident in South Africa (s 246 Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011). (5) Obtain eFiling credentials (username/PIN) and, where goods movement is also conducted, a customs (CD) code.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa has no check-the-box regime: a (Pty) Ltd is statutorily a separate taxpayer subject to corporate income tax (27% for years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023) and cannot elect pass-through treatment. Relevant statutory elections and mandatory classifications: (i) s 24I(4) Income Tax Act 58 of 1962 functional-currency election for foreign-exchange transactions; (ii) corporate-reorganisation elections under ss 42-47 (asset-for-share, amalgamation, intra-group transfers, intra-group loans, liquidation distributions) requiring a 70% 'group of companies' relationship with roll-over relief; (iii) s 11A pre-trade expenditure deduction election; (iv) s 50 VAT Act election enabling associated enterprises to form a single VAT group; (v) micro-business turnover tax election (Sixth Schedule, s 48 ITA) for qualifying entities with annual turnover not exceeding ZAR 1,000,000; (vi) hybrid-debt, hybrid-interest and hybrid-instrument rules (ss 8F, 8FA, 23M and 23N ITA) are mandatory re-characterisation provisions, not elections; (vii) s 11D research-and-development incentive requires prior endorsement by the Department of Science and Innovation and SARS.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) — Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991; ancillary transfer duty and customs/excise duties apply to specific transactions and goods
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: ZAR 1,000,000 compulsory registration (taxable supplies made in the preceding 12 months or reasonably expected in the next 12 months); ZAR 50,000 voluntary registration threshold; non-resident vendors must register where they carry on an 'enterprise' in South Africa (s 23 VAT Act)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No universal real-time fiscal stamping or ex-ante clearance is currently imposed on advisory services in South Africa. VAT vendors must issue s 20-compliant tax invoices (paper or electronic) or combined invoices within 21 days of the time of supply, retain records for 5 years (s 55 VAT Act), and file monthly or two-monthly VAT 201 returns electronically via SARS eFiling. SARS has launched a phased, PEPPOL-based e-Invoicing programme (voluntary onboarding of the large-business segment from 2025 with progressive expansion), coupled with SARS e@sys digital document verification, automatic third-party data matching, and continuous audit analytics. Physical digital tax stamps/permits remain mandatory only for specified excisable goods (e.g., alcoholic beverages and tobacco products); they do not apply to M&A advisory services supplied by a (Pty) Ltd.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: zero-rated under s 11(1)(a) of the VAT Act where the vendor exports the goods physically from South Africa within the prescribed period and retains the export declaration and transport evidence. Services: zero-rated under s 11(2)(l) where supplied to a non-resident who is not in South Africa at the time of supply, and under s 11(2)(m) where the services are supplied directly to a non-resident and the services are consumed or used outside South Africa; the statutory exclusions in s 11(2)(l) (services directly connected with South African land, movable property located in South Africa, or a South African event or performance) must be excluded. For a cross-border M&A advisory boutique, the engagement letter, client board/management situs, decision-making location, governing law, economic benefit and place-of-consumption analysis are the decisive zero-rating determinants; success fees related to acquisitions or divestitures of offshore targets by non-resident clients are generally eligible for the 0% rate where the recipient is outside South Africa and the services are not consumed in South Africa, subject to the s 11(2) exclusions.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD 500 / electronic EEI where goods are exported)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill (proof of physical export of goods)
Inward Remittance Certificate (foreign-currency receipt evidencing settlement from the non-resident client)
Commercial invoice and s 20 VAT tax invoice
Signed engagement letter, underlying transaction agreement, non-resident status evidence and place-of-consumption analysis
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS rigorously audits export zero-rating claims: if goods are not exported within the prescribed period, or the prescribed documents are unavailable, the supply is deemed standard-rated and VAT at 15% is clawed back with additional tax of 10% under s 39 of the VAT Act plus statutory interest. Incorrect refunds attract additional tax under s 60 of the VAT Act (100% of the VAT shortfall; 200% where fraud is involved), understatement penalties under ss 222-223 of the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011 ranging from 10% to 200% of the shortfall (25% for careless conduct or substantial understatement, 50% for no reasonable grounds, 100% for gross negligence, 150-200% for intentional evasion), monthly non-compliance penalties under s 210 TAA, criminal fines of up to ZAR 2,000,000 and imprisonment of up to 3 years under s 234 TAA, and imprisonment of up to 5 years under s 235 TAA for deliberate tax evasion. Export evidence must be retained for 5 years (s 55 VAT Act) and produced on SARS demand; fraudulent or reckless zero-rating claims may also trigger a full enterprise-wide VAT audit, suspension of refunds, and the issue of additional assessments in respect of prior tax periods.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) acting through the Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv); day-to-day execution is delegated to Authorised Dealers (ADs), being registered South African banks bound by the Currency and Exchanges Manual (CEM), the Exchange Control Regulations, 1961 (as amended), and FinSurv circulars.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South African rand (ZAR) is a fully deliverable currency with liberalised current-account convertibility for bona fide service fees, dividends, interest, royalties, and trade-related payments, subject to the provision of supporting documents, FICA-compliant beneficial-ownership verification, and a valid SARS tax-clearance certificate where required by the authorised dealer's risk limits. Capital-account transacting is controlled: inward non-resident investment in a South African (Pty) Ltd is permitted without prior FinSurv approval, provided the inward funds are routed through an authorised dealer, correctly reported under the Balance of Payments (BOP)/CSD-RTT framework, and are not derived from non-compliant sources. Outbound remittances of dividends, loan capital, and shareholders' loans require authorised-dealer verification of the underlying corporate resolution, audited or reviewed financials, tax compliance (dividends tax / interest withholding tax), and, for sums above bank thresholds, a SARS tax-clearance certificate (TC01/TRC). The main practical remittance hurdle for a foreign-owned M&A boutique is not absolute capital controls but documentary integrity: a fully executed engagement agreement, proper invoice trail, proof of economic substance, and a demonstrated absence of structuring solely to circumvent South African exchange-control or tax rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: South Africa does not impose a fixed percentage-based export-proceeds surrender requirement, but residents are obliged to ensure that all export proceeds from services (including cross-border M&A success fees) are received into a South African authorised-dealer account within 180 days of the date of the service invoice or performance. Upon receipt, foreign currency must be converted into ZAR unless the client has obtained an authorised-dealer-approved dispensation or a foreign-currency retention facility (e.g., a status entity or an approved offshore concentration account). Failure to repatriate within the 180-day window must be explained to the authorised dealer, and the bank will require a debtor-ageing analysis and SARS completion declaration to avoid an adverse exchange-control finding. For deal-contingent success fees, the 180-day clock commences from the later of contractual due date or actual closing; practitioners should contemporaneously document closing statements to pre-empt FinSurv queries.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: The Standard Bank of South Africa Limited

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium with material legal constraints. South Africa does not issue electronic-money-institution (EMI) licences, and offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise Business, Payoneer, Airwallex, Currencycloud) are not authorised dealers under the Exchange Control Regulations. Cross-border success-fee collections routed through an unregulated EMI risk breaching the requirement that all foreign-currency transactions be executed via a South African authorised dealer, and may cause inbound receipts to be reclassified as non-compliant capital inflows. Offshore EMIs may, however, be used for ancillary purposes such as receiving low-value referral payments in USD/EUR before conversion via the AD, provided (i) the AD is disclosed as the ultimate settlement channel; (ii) all amounts are fully declared in the company's BOP reporting; and (iii) the company maintains its primary treasury relationship with a regulated South African bank. The authors advise that a South African (Pty) Ltd should not rely on an EMI as its primary cross-border collection rail because FinSurv can refuse to give clearing confirmation to receipts that bypass the national payment system, and FIC-AML exposure increases.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: South African FIC Guidance Notes permit remote corporate onboarding using risk-based measures, including interactive live-video verification, Electronic Know-Your-Customer (e-KYC) tools, and digital submission of CIPC and SARS records. In practice, Tier-1 South African banks require at least one director (or a designated alternate with board authority) holding a valid mandate to complete either an in-branch interview or an interactive virtual interview with the bank's corporate onboarding team. A physical visit to Johannesburg (Sandton/Rosebank) or Cape Town is not a statutory precondition, but banks will likely require notarised/certified passports of all directors and beneficial owners, a CIPC-issued Beneficial Ownership Register extract, and an original or certified copy of the Memorandum of Incorporation and board resolution approving the account mandate. Foreign-resident directors may be onboarded remotely through the bank's secure portal provided the company structure is transparent, the ultimate beneficial owners are natural persons, and the bank's enhanced due diligence (EDD) committee approves the medium-risk classification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident controlling shareholders or a layered ownership structure (trust, offshore holding company, or nominee shareholders) creating uncertainty about the ultimate beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current CIPC Beneficial Ownership Register extract; a diagrammatic ownership chart evidencing every natural person with greater than 5% interest; certified passports of all directors, shareholders, and any protector/trustee; FICA declaration forms; notarised MOI and resolutions; and a beneficial-ownership written attestation signed by the ultimate owner; if using a foreign trust, a trust deed, letter of wishes, trustees' KYC, and source-of-wealth statement for settled funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lumpy, high-value inbound success-fee wires from foreign bidders or sellers that appear inconsistent with the company's projected operating revenue profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully executed engagement letter for the M&A mandate; the underlying sale/purchase agreement signature page and closing statement; board and shareholder resolutions approving the success-fee invoice; the final itemised fee invoice with the deal value and fee percentage; the remitter's bank SWIFT confirmation and source-of-funds letter; bank reference from the foreign counterparty; and the boutique's internally maintained deal log showing milestone delivery and a reconciliatory audit trail from close to receipt.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound payments to non-resident referral partners or co-advisors, creating a potential third-party payment ('pay-through') red flag under FIC section 27 and possible avoidance of tax withholding on commissions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed referral/co-advisory agreement with an itemised fee calculus; the invoice and tax invoice issued by the non-resident beneficiary; a SARS-compliant declaration of any section 35 (State Revenue) or 37A withholding obligations; evidence that the recipient is a genuine service provider (licence, resume, prior invoices); bank confirmation of the recipient's KYC; and a written undertaking that no payment is being made to circumvent exchange controls or sanctions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated (Pty) Ltd with no operating history or audited financial statements, presenting a business-risk and source-of-wealth gap.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Founding shareholder statement of initial capital contribution; bank statement evidencing the capital injection; signed service agreement and pipeline of target mandates; a cash-flow forecast and deal-pipeline abstract (NDA-redacted) supporting expected fee revenue; director CVs and professional references; SARS tax-clearance status (or proof of application); and personal source-of-wealth records for shareholders injecting additional operating funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Deal counterparties that touch or transact through sanctioned, high-risk, or high-monitored jurisdictions (e.g., Russia, Iran, North Korea, or FATF greylist states), triggering sanctions-screening failures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Comprehensive sanctions screening report generated by the bank's screening provider with no unresolved matches; the counterparty's own KYC pack, including passport, incorporation extract, regulatory licence, and ultimate beneficial ownership; contractual sanctions and anti-bribery representations from the counterparty; and, where the deal involves a covered jurisdiction, an OFAC/UN/EU-specific exclusion memo, with documented advice from counsel that the transaction is legally permissible and not facilitating onward trade in prohibited goods or services.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholders subscribe for Pty Ltd shares by wiring funds directly to the company's capital-receipts account at the authorised dealer. The bank records the transfer under the inward-transfer process, assigns the prescribed Balance of Payments (BOP) purpose code for equity capital under the CSD-RTT reporting framework (e.g., code 1100 for inward direct investment — equity), and issues an inward-transfer certificate evidencing the foreign capital in South Africa. The company must provide its board resolution authorising the share issue, the amended memorandum of incorporation if required, the shareholders' register reflecting the subscription, and, where the shareholder is a corporate entity, its constitutional documents and UBO declaration. Loan capital from non-resident shareholders requires a signed loan agreement with an arm's-length interest rate, and must be filed with the authorised dealer for acknowledgement so that future interest and principal repayments can be cleared outward without additional FinSurv approval. To avoid misclassification of the remittance as operating revenue, the investor must state 'CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION — EQUITY' in SWIFT field 70 (Remittance Information) and reference the designated capital account, not the general operational account. For amounts above the bank's threshold, SARS tax-clearance and FICA/UBO documentation will be required before activation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound clearing is executed via SWIFT MT103 through the authorised dealer's nostro network. For an M&A boutique, the principal outbound flows are: (i) success-fee payments to non-resident referral partners, (ii) professional fees to foreign legal and accounting advisors, (iii) data-room and virtual data-room subscriptions, and (iv) deal-related travel and administrative costs. Each payment requires a completed outward-payment instruction with the correct BOP purpose code (e.g., service code 7200 for business/management services or an equivalent professional-services code) and, for payments above the bank's internal threshold, a SARS tax-clearance certificate, the underlying engagement agreement or invoice, proof of service completion, and a declaration confirming the payment is not a disguised outward investment or capital flight. The bank debits the ZAR account and performs the FX conversion at the daily dealing rate, or debits the corresponding foreign-currency sub-account if the company maintains multi-currency accounts. Letters of credit are not relevant to a service-based transaction; the appropriate rail is clean wire transfer (MT103) with full supporting documentation. To reduce FX conversion leakage, the treasury blueprint should maintain ZAR, USD, and EUR accounts at the same authorised dealer, enabling same-day conversion and settlement without intermediary bank delays.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward exchange contracts (FECs) with the authorised dealer covering committed USD or EUR success-fee receivables, with a maximum tenor typically of 12 months, renewable upon re-verification of the underlying deal documentation and subject to the historical-test/(trade-related) rule.
FX swaps (swap deposits) executed with the authorised dealer to match the timing of an anticipated fee receipt with an identified outbound disbursement, structured on a non-speculative basis.

OTC foreign-currency options (call or put) written by the authorised dealer to hedge pipeline deal exposure, provided the notional is capped at the expected fee amount and the option is not used for leveraged speculation.

Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCIRS), permissible only where the company has long-dated foreign-currency debt or material funding liabilities, and then only with the authorisation of the dealer and, where required, FinSurv clearance; not a standard instrument for advisory-fee treasury management.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs): not permitted onshore as a primary hedging tool because ZAR is a fully deliverable currency; any NDF use would require an express FinSurv dispensation demonstrating an inability to execute a deliverable contract in the relevant currency pair, and is therefore excluded from the standard toolkit.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CIPC Annual Return (AR) with Public Interest Score (PIS) schedule under s.33 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), Pretoria, South Africa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts an administrative penalty of ZAR 500 (approximately USD 27) per return. Failure to submit annual returns for two or more consecutive years is a statutory trigger for a s.82(3) deregistration notice and administrative strike-off of the company from the CIPC register; directors may subsequently lose limited-liability protection for company obligations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (AFS) filed to the CIPC in XBRL under s.30 and s.31 of the Companies Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: CIPC (submitted concurrently with the Annual Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the company's financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A CIPC administrative penalty of up to ZAR 10,000 may be imposed for non-filing; continuous default constitutes a ground for deregistration, and directors are personally exposed under s.88 for knowingly approving false or misleading financial records.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Company Income Tax return (ITR14) with supporting schedules including taxable income and capital gains computations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) via eFiling
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the company's financial year-end under the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A tiered administrative non-compliance penalty under s.210 of the Tax Administration Act applies monthly until filing (up to ZAR 16,000 per month based on turnover); unpaid tax bears monthly prescribed interest of approximately 10% to 10.5% per annum; non-compliance following a final demand exposes assets to SARS collection measures and possible criminal referral.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership (BO) Register data confirmation attached to the Annual Return under the new Part D of Chapter III of the Companies Act, as amended in 2023
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: CIPC (integrated into the annual return filing portal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually with the Annual Return; updated filing within 10 business days of any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Strict civil and criminal liability under the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022: fines up to ZAR 1,000,000 (approximately USD 54,000) and/or imprisonment up to 60 months; the CIPC will reject the Annual Return until BO data is confirmed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: EMP501 final annual employer reconciliation submitting IRP5 and IT3(a) certificates where the company operates a payroll
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after the employer tax year-end; final filing by 31 May for the standard 28 February tax year and interim filing by 31 October
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly administrative penalties under s.210 of the Tax Administration Act for outstanding EMP501 filings (up to ZAR 16,000); incorrect PAYE/UIF/SDL declarations produce assessments with late-payment penalties of 10% per annum on understated amounts.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit is compulsory if the Public Interest Score (PIS) is 350 or above; PIS is calculated under Companies Regulation 25(3) as 1 point per employee, 10 points per ZAR 1 million of turnover, 1 point per ZAR 1 million of third-party liabilities, and 5 points for any Companies Act non-compliance during the financial year. In addition, this FAIS-regulated M&A advisory boutique operating as a Category I financial services provider must be audited as a condition of its FSCA licence; companies with a PIS between 100 and 349 require an independent review unless shareholders elect a full audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for SMEs (South Africa) applies to a non-public-interest (Pty) Ltd; full IFRS as issued by the IASB is mandatory for public-interest companies, companies with a PIS of 350 or above, and FSCA financial-services licence submissions; CIPC accepts the AFS filing in XBRL under either framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must keep a Register of Beneficial Ownership at its registered office and must file the register data with CIPC as a mandatory component of the Annual Return. Each annual confirmation requires a declaration of the current beneficial owners, capturing individuals or legal persons holding 25%-plus of the economic interest, voting rights, or effective control; the register must be updated at CIPC within 10 business days of any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership. As an accountable institution under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act with a Medium-Risk Enhanced AML profile, the company must retain verified identification, source-of-funds, and client due-diligence records supporting each confirmation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Securities (where any class of shares is issued)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 320 - 1,080 per annum (ZAR 6,000 - 20,000) covering a CIPC-registered office, company secretarial maintenance and preparation and submission of annual returns and XBRL filings
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,700 - 6,500 per annum (ZAR 50,000 - 120,000) for a compulsory FAIS/statutory audit of this M&A advisory boutique, varying with transaction flow, success-fee revenue and review of related-party disclosures

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% (years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023; formerly 28%)
